Here's the reasoning: Awaken the Woods has a mana cost of {X}{G}{G}. When you cast it, you first choose a value for X. With X=0, the mana cost is {0}{G}{G}, which is {G}{G}. Your cost reduction effect makes your green spells cost {1} less. According to rule 118.7a, effects that reduce a cost by an amount of generic mana affect only the generic mana component. Since the mana cost {G}{G} has a generic mana component of {0}, the reduction has nothing to reduce. The total cost before Trinisphere is still {G}{G}. Trinisphere's effect then applies because the mana component of the cost ({G}{G}) is less than three mana. Trinisphere makes the spell cost three mana to cast. The cost becomes three mana, which must include the colored mana requirements. You must pay {G}{G} for the two green mana symbols, and you need one additional mana of any color or colorless to reach three total mana. Therefore, the total cost is {G}{G} plus one generic mana, which can be written as {1}{G}{G}. You pay this cost, and since X=0, you create zero 1/1 green Forest Dryad land creature tokens.

To get tokens, you must choose X=1 or more. If you choose X=1, the mana cost is {1}{G}{G}. Your cost reduction reduces the generic mana component by {1}, making it {0}{G}{G}. Trinisphere then checks the mana component, which is now {G}{G} (two mana), and increases it to three mana. The cost becomes {1}{G}{G} again. You would pay {1}{G}{G} and create one token. For any X >= 1, the cost reduction will first reduce the generic mana component (X) by 1, and then Trinisphere will ensure the total mana paid is at least three.
